featured_videos.title: Christina Applegate, Please Go Carnivore
featured_videos.creator: Boston Carnivore Diane Ladd
featured_videos.commentary: The comments on this one hit different because people aren't just cheering for a celebrity, they're actually sharing what worked for them. That husband with MS whose pain dropped, the person who went from raw vegan to carnivore and lost the joint pain in days, the woman who reached out to Christina's publicist. this isn't noise, it's people who've lived it trying to pass on what they know. The tricky part is that reaching someone like Christina means cutting through decades of conventional advice she's probably gotten from every angle, but when you've got real people saying "my lesions showed up on MRI and then everything changed," that carries weight her doctors might not expect.

featured_videos.title: So Carnivores Are Eating Fruit Now! No Longer Carnivore?
featured_videos.creator: Happy Healthy Vegan
featured_videos.editorial_title: So Carnivores Are Eating Fruit Now! No Longer Carnivore?
featured_videos.commentary:
Look, the comment section here is wild, but let me be straight with you: people eating meat-based food who then add some fruit aren't "quitting carnivore" any more than someone who does two meals instead of three is. The carnivore world is big enough for different approaches, and honestly, some people do better with a little seasonal fruit. That's just their biology, not a moral failing.

What I find more interesting is the rebranding language that gets people's backs up. If someone wants to add berries or melon to an otherwise meat-based diet, just say that. You don't have to call it "animal-based fruit" to make it fit. The community's frustration in these comments isn't really about the fruit. it's about the goalpost moving without anyone admitting the posts moved. That's fair to call out.

Here's what matters: does it work for that person's health, energy, and results? If yes, great. If they're changing their approach because the first version stopped working, that's valuable data, not betrayal. I've coached enough people to know that the version you can stick with beats the perfect version you quit in three weeks. Some people thrive on just meat. Some people thrive on meat plus a bit of fruit. Both are true.

featured_videos.title: Processed Meats Will Kill You? I read every ingredient.
featured_videos.creator: KenDBerryMD
featured_videos.editorial_title: Processed Meats Will Kill You? I read every ingredient.
featured_videos.commentary: Ken's landing on something the community keeps bringing up: budget carnivore isn't about being perfect, it's about being better than the alternative. The comment from the person spending $150 per paycheck on food for two people isn't looking for grass-fed ribeye. they're looking for real protein that doesn't come in a box of Ultra-Processed Carbs, and that matters way more than the ingredient label police want to admit. You'll notice nobody in these comments is sick or regretful about the hot dogs and spam; they're grateful the permission slip exists. That's the actual conversation happening, not the "processed meat bad" headline most health media runs with.

featured_videos.title: Proper Carnivore Bacon Cheeseburger Pie
featured_videos.creator: Coach Carnivore Cam
featured_videos.commentary: What strikes me most about this thread is how many people are already doing variations of this. The comment about tailgate football and sausage wings, the folks mentioning they've made something similar, the person wanting to add pickled jalapeños. that's the real carnivore community right there. You're not inventing from scratch, you're showing people how to take what they already know works and layer it into something that doesn't feel like eating the same thing for the hundredth time. That boredom problem is real, and it's usually what trips people up after month three or four. A pie like this. built on eggs, beef, cheese, cream. it's just meat and fat dressed up differently, which means it's still doing the metabolic work but your brain doesn't get tired of it. The fact that people are excited to make this for their families tells you everything you need to know about whether variation matters for staying consistent long-term.

featured_videos.title: The Worst Part of Carnivore Isn't the Food
featured_videos.creator: Literal Meathead
featured_videos.editorial_title: The Worst Part of Carnivore Isn't the Food
featured_videos.commentary: The isolation piece hits different, doesn't it. You're over a year in, feeling better than you have in decades, and your own family still treats it like a phase or a problem to solve. That comment about watching loved ones stay stuck on medications while munching "poison" captures something real that nobody warns you about when you start. the loneliness of seeing what works for your body and feeling helpless watching everyone else dismiss it. The fiber lectures, the worried calls, the skeptical silence at dinner. That's the actual tax of this way of eating, and it's not about willpower or macros. It's about being on the other side of something and realizing most people aren't ready to look. Worth sitting with that one instead of just celebrating the weight loss.

featured_videos.title: I Tried Seasoning and It Cost Me 9 Pounds and My Drive | Lion Diet Refresh Day 112-118
featured_videos.creator: Ferrigno Freedom
featured_videos.editorial_title: I Tried Seasoning and It Cost Me 9 Pounds and My Drive | Lion Diet Refresh Day 112-118
featured_videos.commentary: The 9-pound swing is water and glycogen, full stop, and it tells you something important: your nervous system was genuinely calmer on plain meat. That's not placebo. One commenter said "carbs affect my ambitions big time" and another talked about their brain finally settling down after cutting sugar, and that's the thing people miss when they're focusing on the scale. Your body was telling you something real. The seasoning itself wasn't the villain, it was the plant compounds triggering inflammation or histamine response in someone who's been strict long enough that their system got quiet. Go back to salt and meat, your drive will come back, and honestly, that's your answer. Not forever, just for now.
